name: libft
tagline: My own C library, rewritten from scratch.
pitch: The standard C functions, rebuilt one by one. The toolbox every other 42 project is built on.
illustration_alt: The functions of libft grouped into libc, additional and linked-list functions

features.title: Libc, rewritten
features.text: strlen, memcpy, atoi, calloc… the same behaviour as the originals, written without the standard library.

features.title: Extra helpers
features.text: split, itoa, strjoin, strtrim: the functions the libc is missing for everyday string work.

features.title: Linked lists
features.text: A small t_list toolkit to create, add, map, iterate and free lists without leaks.

options.text: Header with every prototype and the t_list struct.
Static archive to link into your program.
Builds libft.a. Also: clean, fclean, re.

binary_note: Download the archive, write a small main.c that includes libft.h, and link them together.

name: ft_printf
pitch: printf, rebuilt with variadic arguments. Eight conversions, one return value, zero surprises.
illustration_alt: The eight ft_printf conversions and an example output for each

features.title: Variadic arguments
features.text: Reads any number of arguments with va_start, va_arg and va_end.

features.title: Eight conversions
features.text: c, s, p, d, i, u, x, X and %, each printed exactly like the real printf.

features.title: Same return value
features.text: Returns the number of characters printed, so it can replace printf in tests.

options.text: A character, a string.
A pointer address in hexadecimal.
Signed and unsigned decimal numbers.
Hex in lower or upper case, and a literal %.

binary_note: The test binary prints every conversion next to the real printf so you can compare.

name: get_next_line
tagline: Read a file line by line, with no memory leaks.
pitch: Call it, get the next line. Works on files and standard input, with any buffer size.
illustration_alt: A file read one line at a time by get_next_line, with the second line highlighted

features.title: One line per call
features.text: Each call returns the next line, including its \n, or NULL at the end of the file.

features.title: A static buffer
features.text: Whatever was read past the line is kept for the next call.

features.title: Any BUFFER_SIZE
features.text: From 1 to 10 000 000 bytes, chosen at compile time, with no leaks.

options.text: A file descriptor: a file opened with open(), or 0 for standard input.
Bytes read per read() call. Set with -D BUFFER_SIZE=42.
The line read, or NULL at end of file or on error.

binary_note: The demo binary prints a file line by line, numbering each call.

name: push_swap
tagline: Sort a stack with the fewest operations possible.
pitch: Two stacks, eleven moves, and one goal: sort the numbers in as few operations as possible.
illustration_alt: Stack a before sorting, unordered, and after sorting, in order

features.title: Two stacks
features.text: Numbers start in stack a. Stack b is empty and used as temporary space.

features.title: Eleven operations
features.text: Swap, push, rotate and reverse rotate, on one stack or both at once.

features.title: As few as possible
features.text: The program prints the shortest list of operations it finds to sort stack a.

options.text: Swap the first two numbers of a, b, or both.
Push the top number from one stack to the other.
Rotate: the first number goes to the bottom.
Reverse rotate: the last number comes to the top.

binary_note: Give it a list of integers, without duplicates, and it prints the operations that sort them.

name: so_long
tagline: A small 2D game built with the MiniLibX.
pitch: Pick up every item on the map, then reach the exit. Every move is counted.
illustration_alt: A pixel-art level of so_long with walls, collectibles, the player and the exit

features.title: Maps in .ber files
features.text: A rectangle of characters: walls, floor, items, one exit and one player.

features.title: Valid paths only
features.text: The map is checked: closed by walls, with a path to every item and to the exit.

features.title: Every move counted
features.text: The move count is shown in the shell. Escape or the red cross closes the game.

options.text: Wall and empty floor.
Collectible: pick them all up to open the exit.
The exit and the player start.
Move. Escape quits the game.

binary_note: Download the game, then launch it with one of the maps in the maps/ folder.

name: born2beroot
tagline: Setting up and securing a Debian server.
pitch: A Debian virtual machine, set up by hand and locked down layer by layer.
illustration_alt: The layers of the born2beroot server, from Debian up to the monitoring script

features.title: Encrypted partitions
features.text: LVM on an encrypted disk, with separate partitions for /, /home, /var and more.

features.title: Locked-down access
features.text: SSH on port 4242 only, no root login, UFW firewall, strict sudo rules.

features.title: Monitoring
features.text: A script broadcasts CPU, memory, disk and network usage to every terminal every 10 minutes.

options.text: Firewall: only port 4242 is open.
Every command logged, 3 password attempts max.
Expire every 30 days, 10 characters minimum.
Runs monitoring.sh every 10 minutes.
